advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Signal (stderr warning and/or non-zero-ish handling) when a successful prune cannot write its durable audit line, rather than silently returning 0 as if the record were written.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/bridge_repair.py:62-68: `if path is None: return None` and `except OSError: return None` — both failure modes are swallowed

src/rebar/_commands/bridge_repair.py:223-229: `audit_file = _record_audit(...)` then `if audit_file: print(...)` and unconditional `return 0` — the mutation via save() has already happened at line 208
docs/user-guide.md:411-413: '...each run appends a durable record (actor, deleted keys, before/after counts) to `rebar-bridge-repair-audit.jsonl`...' stated as an unconditional guarantee
ABSENCE: no warning is emitted to stderr and no exit-code change when the audit line cannot be written after a mutation succeeded
advisory.finding: A successful prune can complete with no durable audit record and no operator signal: _record_audit()/_audit_path() silently return None when the tracker has no resolvable git dir or when the append raises OSError, yet prune_orphan_reverse_bindings still returns exit 0 and prints a success message. This contradicts the documented guarantee that 'each run appends a durable record'.
scenarios: Tracker directory whose .git resolution yields empty string (bare checkout / unusual layout) → _audit_path returns None → prune mutates and reports success with no audit line
Git dir present but not writable (permissions, full disk) → OSError swallowed → same silent outcome
advisory.suggested_fix: When save() succeeded but _record_audit returned None, emit a clear stderr warning naming the missing audit path; consider whether an un-auditable successful mutation should exit 2 or at least warn loudly.
